title: Synthesizers
objective: After this level you can explain how a synthesizer makes sound.
summary: A synth's oscillator sets pitch, its filter removes harmonics to shape timbre, and its envelope (ADSR) shapes loudness. Moog unveiled his modular synth in 1964; the Minimoog came in 1970.

cards.headline: A synthesizer makes a note out of electricity alone.
cards.body: No string vibrates, no pipe fills with air. Inside, circuits manipulate electrical currents to generate a sound, which a speaker finally turns into air pressure. Three parts do the shaping, and each is a knob you can learn to hear.

cards.headline: The oscillator sets the pitch
cards.body: An oscillator makes a repeating electrical wave. Remember Level 3: pitch is frequency, how many times per second something vibrates. On Robert Moog's synthesizer, pressing a key sent the oscillator a voltage that depended on which key you pressed, and that set the pitch. Some wave shapes are rich: a sawtooth wave contains all the harmonics of its note, higher frequencies stacked on top. That gives the next step something to carve.

cards.headline: The filter carves the tone
cards.body: Next comes the filter, which removes some of those harmonics. It changes the note's color, what musicians call timbre, while the oscillator keeps the pitch. Starting from a rich wave and filtering part of it away is called subtractive synthesis. Think of a sculptor with a block of marble: the sound is in there, and the filter chips away the rest.

mascot.line: Don't mix these two up: the oscillator sets the pitch, the filter changes the color.

cards.headline: The envelope shapes the note in time
cards.body: Last, an envelope controls how loud the note is from moment to moment, in four stages. Attack: the rise when you press the key. Decay: the fall to a steady level. Sustain: that level, held while your finger stays down. Release: the fade after you let go. Stretch out the attack and the note swells in gently instead of starting at full volume.

questions.prompt: In what year did Robert Moog unveil his modular synthesizer?

options.rationale: Much too early for Moog's instrument.
By then the Minimoog was already years old.

questions.explanation: Moog unveiled his Modular System in October 1964; Switched-On Bach followed in 1968.

questions.prompt: A synth player wants the same note to sound less buzzy without changing its pitch. Which part should they adjust?

options.label: The envelope's release
options.rationale: Release only changes how the note fades out.

options.label: The keyboard
options.rationale: A different key means a different pitch.

questions.explanation: The filter removes harmonics to change the timbre, while the oscillator keeps the pitch.

questions.prompt: You press a higher key on a Moog. In Level 3's terms, what changes?

options.label: The filter removes more harmonics
options.rationale: The filter shapes timbre, not pitch.

options.label: The oscillator's wave repeats more times per second, so the pitch rises
The envelope's attack gets faster
options.rationale: The envelope shapes loudness over time.

options.label: The sound travels faster to your ear
options.rationale: Sound's speed doesn't depend on pitch.

questions.explanation: Each key sends the oscillator a different voltage, setting its frequency, which you hear as pitch.
